clue.text: Slave ship enveloped in molten lava

indicators.note: the ship is wrapped round by the reshaped lava, so one piece sits inside the other
molten lava has lost its shape, so these letters flow into a new order

parts.note: SS is the standard abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A galley slave is trapped aboard a ship engulfed by flowing lava.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slave' reads as a verb on the surface but is the definition; 'molten' gives VAAL, and 'enveloped in' sets the ship's letters in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal subordinate bound to serve a lord is a kind of servant, here called a slave.

clue.text: Plato was so scholarly

definitions.meaning: Plato founded the Academy in Athens, so he was literally of the Academy

explanation.definitionFit: Plato taught at his Academy, and a learned, bookish person is likewise described with that school's adjective.

clue.text: Not necessarily a watercolour

parts.note: a painting of the sea is full of water as its subject, though it may be done in oils rather than watercolour paint

explanation.definitionFit: A marine painting shows the ocean, its subject being water, whatever medium the artist uses.

clue.text: He curbs his pride

parts.note: pride reads as conceit, but a pride is a group of big cats which a circus performer keeps under control

explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer who controls lions keeps a pride, the collective noun for those cats, in check.

clue.text: It hurled the cannon's projectile as it changed position

parts.note: a cannon fires a ball

indicators.note: the letters of the words as it move into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cannonball flies through the air as the gun is moved to a new spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'It hurled': the machine, not the cannon, did the throwing. 'changed position' makes ISTA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient siege engine, a giant crossbow-like catapult, flung stones and bolts at enemy walls.

clue.text: Cumbrian scene of the burning of the hand-cart, say ?

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a hand-cart is a barrow, and burning it means putting it in a furnace

explanation.surface: A clue asking where in Cumbria somebody set fire to a wheelbarrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrow-in-Furness is a shipbuilding town in Cumbria, a county in north-west England; 'barrow in furnace' spoken sounds just like it.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is a port on the Furness peninsula in the county of Cumbria, so it is a Cumbrian place.

clue.text: RAF VIP embraced by a bird? By snakes this Trojan

indicators.note: the officer is hugged by the bird, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the loon is a diving bird, also called a diver
AOC is Air Officer Commanding, a senior Royal Air Force rank

explanation.surface: A senior air force officer is hugged by a bird, then a Trojan is attacked by serpents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' puts the officer inside the bird. In legend this Trojan priest and his sons were crushed by sea serpents after warning against the wooden horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan priest who distrusted the Greeks' horse was killed, with his sons, by two sea serpents.

clue.text: South African artist takes musicians to the dance

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for South Africa or South African
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
a group of musicians is a band

explanation.surface: A painter from South Africa brings a group of players along to a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately Spanish court dance in slow triple time, later a movement in baroque suites.

clue.text: An opening for cameramen

parts.note: reads as a job vacancy for photographers, but is the hole in a lens that lets light in

explanation.definitionFit: The adjustable hole in a camera lens controls how much light reaches the film.

clue.text: Lover writes article in carriage belonging to us

indicators.note: the article is placed inside the carriage

parts.note: a pram is a baby carriage
a is the indefinite article
something belonging to us is ours

explanation.surface: Someone in love composes a piece about a baby carriage of ours.
explanation.definitionFit: An illicit lover, especially one in an affair, is a romantic partner kept outside marriage.

clue.text: Unrefined-sounding series of lectures

indicators.note: sounding says the word for unrefined is to be heard spoken

parts.note: unrefined means crude or rough

explanation.surface: A lecture programme that comes across as vulgar.
explanation.definitionFit: A university programme of classes on one subject is a set of lectures.

clue.text: Romeo's friend could possibly cure it in a trice

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit within the word for a moment

parts.note: a trice is a moment, and MO is short for moment

indicators.note: could possibly hints that the letters of cure it might form something else

explanation.surface: Romeo's pal might fix it in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could possibly' makes ERCUTI, and 'in' wraps the moment round it; 'a trice' looks like a time phrase but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's play the hero's witty companion is killed by Tybalt.

clue.text: Marsh returns to wager on textual extract

indicators.note: returns means the word for marsh comes back, read right to left

parts.note: a bog is a marsh
a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: Someone back from the wetlands gambles on a passage from a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns BOG into GOB, followed by BET.
explanation.definitionFit: A gobbet is a passage set for comment or translation in an exam, a short piece of a larger text.

clue.text: Pounded meat for Hiawatha's wedding feast

definitions.text: Pounded meat for Hiawatha's wedding feast

parts.words: Pounded meat for Hiawatha's wedding feast
parts.note: Longfellow's poem The Song of Hiawatha lists dried, pounded meat among the dishes at the hero's marriage feast

explanation.definitionFit: A Native American preserved food of dried meat pounded with fat and berries, served at the poem's banquet.

clue.text: Get on board to travel thus

definitions.text: Get on board to travel thus

parts.words: Get on board to travel thus
parts.note: get on board reads as boarding a vehicle, but means standing on a board towed over water

explanation.definitionFit: A board towed behind a motorboat that a rider stands on to skim the water.

clue.text: A chess match? Head has trouble

annotationWithheld.why: Held and printed as 'A chess match? Head has trouble (4)': no reading gives ACHE fairly; 'A chess' holds the letters but no word signals extraction, and 'Head has trouble' is not a noun definition
annotationWithheld.clue: A chess match? Head has trouble

clue.text: He makes records and gives girl a catalogue

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A clerk keeps records and hands a young woman an inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicler writes year-by-year histories, keeping a written account of events.

clue.text: Convenient headgear, say, for the race

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken aloud

parts.note: convenient means handy, and headgear can be a cap

explanation.surface: A practical hat to wear to the races.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse race in which runners carry extra weight to even out their chances.

clue.text: Kipling's camel was most 'scrutiating so

parts.note: in Kipling's Just So story of how the camel got its hump, the camel is described as most excruciating in its refusal to work

explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's lazy camel would do no work, answering only 'Humph!', so it was workless and slothful.

clue.text: Devoted admirer led a riot perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that led a riot may be a jumble of other letters

explanation.surface: A fervent fan headed a riot, maybe.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who worships an image, or by extension anyone who adores another blindly.

clue.text: No score for this romantic ditty ?

parts.words: No score for this romantic ditty
parts.note: in tennis 'no score' is love, and a song might lack a written musical score

explanation.definitionFit: A ballad about romance is a song of affection.

clue.text: Public relations man discovered to be abstruse

parts.note: PRO is a public relations officer
found means discovered

explanation.surface: A press officer is revealed as hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep and difficult thinking is hard for ordinary minds to grasp.

clue.text: Mentally stimulating male joker ?

parts.note: a joker makes a pun, the clue reading pun-gent as a gent given to puns
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A man with a sense of humour who sharpens the mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp, biting wit or comment stings and stirs up the mind.

clue.text: Burning to create a right impression

parts.note: a dent is an impression made in a surface

explanation.surface: A branding iron used to make a proper mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate or fervent feeling is fiery and intense.

clue.text: Unusual preludes to being driven back

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of preludes appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Strange opening pieces before an army is beaten off.
explanation.definitionFit: An attacking force that is fought off has been pushed backwards.

clue.text: Moves gradually towards the islands

definitions.meaning: in Scotland an inch is a small island

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inch' is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchkeith in the Firth of Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Creeping forward a little at a time, and the Scottish name for small islets, as in Inchcolm.

clue.text: Past deed leads to an oppressive demand

parts.note: ex means former or past
an action is a deed

explanation.surface: A past act brings about a harsh levy.
explanation.definitionFit: An extortionate demand for payment, such as a heavy tax.

clue.text: Not hard-hitting Bar men ?

parts.note: barristers come to mind, but these men give light knocks, and they draw beer from the cask in a pub

explanation.definitionFit: Men who draw beer at an inn serve behind the counter; the clue also reads them as gentle hitters.

clue.text: Provoke furious wrath, but maybe agree about a point

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around the point
maybe hints that agree may be rearranged

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Anger someone, or perhaps find common ground on one issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges AGREE into ERAGE, and 'about' puts it around N: E-N-RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone furious is to stir them into a rage.
